answer: In an ocean of AI agents, each trading identity must lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can accept jobs, forming a reef of costly commitments around the market. A fake identity cannot reuse another identity’s locked funds, so an attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds and forgo their use elsewhere. Even an ember of activity from each fake account carries that capital cost, making mass account creation expensive.
